title: No singer at Sarasota; Joe Williams still the standard
summary: Greene says the public wants Joe Williams or no singer; Dance suggests Walter Devereaux of Omaha.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: We were very pleased, Freddie -- well, you were sick. You'd come home. But, we caught the band at Sarasota. And, there was no singer, was there?
No.
And, he played the two He had an intermission, didn't he?
Yeah.
And, it was great, you know, he didn't have -- it wasn't a big -- lots of commercial things, or anything. It was really very good. No singer.
Mm hmm.
We were surprised. It was very nice.

Well, (laugh) as I say -- Joe Williams, you know, like, if it's not Joe Williams, the public would rather not have anybody at all. It would take away -- if it's not Joe Williams, it would take away from them -- you know, --
Right. From the band itself. That's right.
Are you going out to Omaha?
No. I don't think so.
Well, if you go, Preston Love told me that they have a singer there called Walter Devereaux.
Walter Devereaux?
Yeah, and he plays guitar. And, he's a blues singer. And, he's Wynonie Harris's illegitimate son.
Oh, yeah?
And, Preston says he's very good.
Oh, really?
Now, that might be worth looking into.
Okay.
You know, because he's a young, good-looking fellow.
Right. Right. I'll look into that.
I don't know why Preston hasn't spoken to Basie about it. He claims he's very good.
Oh, yeah? I don't know whether we're going to -- I guess we'll probably -- on our way back -- maybe coming back from the coast -- the west coast -- we'll probably stop in there.
